title: Book 02 — Introduction: Revised Exam Questions and Model Answers

source.title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
source.author: Ayatullah Murtadha Mutahhari
source.method: Questions were checked against the original Al-Islam.org introduction. The answers distinguish contextual practices from permanent religious principles and preserve the author's qualifications about reported hadith counts.

revision_policy: Keep the introduction focused on taqiyyah, apparent differences among the Imams, contextual interpretation, and the essence of religion.
Do not turn the author’s reported hadith count into a personally verified count.
Explain examples through their underlying purpose and historical context.
Distinguish conventional reconciliation of reports from altering permanent religious principles.

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: What problem does Mutahhari identify in comparing the conduct of Imam al-Husayn with that of the other Imams?
questions.answer: Mutahhari says that people often view Imam al-Husayn’s uprising as contradictory to the conduct of the other Imams, who generally practised taqiyyah and did not rise in the same way. This creates confusion for followers who regard the sayings and actions of all the infallible Imams as authoritative examples. If one Imam rose against a ruler while others practised dissimulation, followers may wonder which conduct they should follow. Mutahhari argues that the apparent differences must be studied through jurisprudence, theology, and the circumstances of each Imam’s time rather than treated as contradictions.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — Why the Imams’ different approaches can appear contradictory

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: How does Mutahhari describe the relationship between taqiyyah and the conduct of the Imams?
questions.answer: Mutahhari says that the Imams generally acted according to taqiyyah during their lives, while Imam al-Husayn chose not to practise dissimulation and instead rose against the corrupt government. This raises two questions: if taqiyyah was justified, why did Imam al-Husayn not use it when the grounds appeared to exist; and if it was not justified, why did the other Imams practise it and instruct their followers to do so? Mutahhari presents these questions as a serious issue that must be examined rather than answered by assuming that one Imam’s conduct invalidates another’s.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — Why the Imams’ different approaches can appear contradictory

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: Why does Mutahhari reject the idea that taqiyyah is an exclusively Shi‘ah practice?
questions.answer: Mutahhari argues that dissimulation under pressure is not unique to Shi‘ahs. He compares it with claims about alteration of the Qur’an: if one group were capable of such an act, members of another group would also be capable of it; the number of people does not change according to sectarian identity. He uses the comparison to show that concealment under pressure is a human response and cannot be treated as an exclusive feature of Shi‘ism. His main purpose is to prevent the discussion of taqiyyah from becoming a sectarian accusation rather than an examination of its religious and practical basis.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — Why the Imams’ different approaches can appear contradictory

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: What does Mutahhari say about the richness of Shi‘ah hadith literature, especially al-Kafi?
questions.answer: Mutahhari says that Shi‘ahs possess a large body of traditions and valuable supplications transmitted from the Prophet and the Imams. He notes that people who have compared the six major Sunni hadith collections with al-Kafi have said that al-Kafi contains more than sixteen thousand traditions. He explicitly says that he has not counted the number himself and is reporting what others have said. He regards this abundance as a major resource for Islamic learning, because the sayings and practices of the Imams provide guidance across many areas of religious life.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — How a rich tradition can guide followers and still require careful interpretation

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: Why can a large number of traditions and different examples from the Imams become a difficulty if they are not carefully studied?
questions.answer: Mutahhari says that abundant traditions are a strength, but they can also create confusion if apparent differences between the Imams are not examined. People may take a particular action from one Imam and treat it as a universal rule, while ignoring the circumstances that shaped it. Others may use selected traditions to justify their own interests and mislead followers. Without research and reconciliation, the abundance of evidence can produce confusion, extremism, and a lack of shared moral direction. Mutahhari therefore argues that the richness of the tradition must be accompanied by careful interpretation and a clear understanding of the principles behind each action.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — How a rich tradition can guide followers and still require careful interpretation

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: What is the purpose of Mutahhari’s comparison between an Imam who lives for twenty to thirty years and one who lives for 250 years?
questions.answer: Mutahhari asks readers to imagine that an infallible leader lives among people for only twenty or thirty years, compared with the same leader living for 250 years and facing many different circumstances. A shorter period may not reveal enough examples for people to distinguish permanent religious principles from actions required by a particular time. A much longer life would expose followers to many more situations and show how the same religious principles are applied differently as circumstances change. The thought experiment explains why the different lives of the Imams are a source of guidance rather than a weakness or contradiction.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — How a rich tradition can guide followers and still require careful interpretation

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: What does Mutahhari mean by distinguishing the essence of religion from the exigencies of a particular time?
questions.answer: Mutahhari says that some actions of a Prophet or Imam respond to the practical needs of the period in which they live, while other teachings express permanent religious principles. Followers must not automatically treat every historical habit or circumstance as an eternal command. By comparing the conduct of several Imams across different periods, one can identify what belongs to the essence of religion and what was appropriate to a specific time. This distinction allows believers to preserve the spirit of Islam without turning temporary practices into rigid rules for every society and era.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — How a rich tradition can guide followers and still require careful interpretation

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: Why did Sufyan al-Thawri object to Imam al-Sadiq’s fine clothing?
questions.answer: Sufyan al-Thawri visited Imam al-Sadiq and criticized him for wearing fine clothing, arguing that the Prophet had lived simply and had not worn such garments. Sufyan assumed that the Prophet’s personal lifestyle should be copied in every age as a fixed religious command. Imam al-Sadiq rejected that assumption and explained that people must use wisdom and consider time and place. The Prophet’s modest lifestyle reflected the social and economic conditions of his era and his commitment to equality and compassion, not a universal rule requiring every Muslim to wear the same kind of clothing forever.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — Imam al-Sadiq on clothing, circumstance, and the spirit of religion

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: How did Imam al-Sadiq explain the Prophet’s simple lifestyle to Sufyan al-Thawri?
questions.answer: Imam al-Sadiq explained that the Prophet’s way of dressing was appropriate to the economic and social conditions of his time. The Prophet lived at a middle-class level and did not use his leadership to take advantage of the wealth and gifts people would have gladly given him. Islam’s permanent commands concern justice, equality, sympathy, and compassion, not a fixed choice between old and fine clothing. The Imam said that people may choose different kinds of clothing as long as they fulfil their responsibilities toward others and do not use wealth in a way that harms or humiliates the poor. The spirit of religion is therefore more important than copying a temporary outward form.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — Imam al-Sadiq on clothing, circumstance, and the spirit of religion

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: What did Imam al-Sadiq do during a famine to show that his comfortable lifestyle did not contradict the Prophet’s compassion and equality?
questions.answer: Mutahhari says that during a famine, Imam al-Sadiq instructed his financial supervisor to sell the family’s stored wheat in the market and buy their daily bread from the same market. The bread available to ordinary people was made from a mixture of oat and wheat, so the Imam chose to eat the same kind of bread. He explained that Islam does not prescribe a particular grain or type of bread; it requires fairness, justice, and kindness in the way people live among others. The story shows that the Imam’s fine clothing or comfortable home did not mean that he ignored the suffering of the poor.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — Imam al-Sadiq on clothing, circumstance, and the spirit of religion

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: Why did Imam ‘Ali not dye his white beard even though he narrated the Prophet’s instruction to dye white hair?
questions.answer: Mutahhari says that Imam ‘Ali narrated the Prophet’s instruction to dye white hair so that Muslims would not resemble the Jews, but ‘Ali himself did not act upon it. He explained that the instruction had been specific to the Prophet’s time and served as a military tactic: during war, dyeing white hair made it harder for the enemy to distinguish older men from younger soldiers. In a later period, the same practice was no longer required for that purpose. The example shows that a Prophetic instruction may sometimes be connected to a specific circumstance rather than establishing a permanent rule for every person and era.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — Imam ‘Ali’s explanation of the beard-dyeing instruction

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: What is meant by conventional reconciliation, or al-jam‘ al-‘urfi, in the context of apparently conflicting traditions?
questions.answer: Mutahhari refers to the conventional reconciliation of apparently conflicting traditions as al-jam‘ al-‘urfi. It means examining the context, purpose, and circumstances of different reports so that they can be understood together rather than treating them as irreconcilable contradictions. A practice may have been required in one time or situation but not in another. By identifying the underlying purpose, scholars can distinguish permanent religious principles from temporary responses to particular conditions. Mutahhari says that this method requires careful research and attention to the circumstances in which the Imams acted.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — Why inherited custom is not automatically a religious obligation

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: Which religious teachings does Mutahhari regard as permanent and unchangeable, unlike actions that depend on the circumstances of a time?
questions.answer: Mutahhari distinguishes temporary practices from the essence of religious teachings, which he describes as divine collective commands based on high and public interests. These commands are not altered simply because society or historical conditions change. As long as human beings exist, the fundamental religious principles that guide human life remain in force. By contrast, some outward actions—such as the Prophet’s clothing or the instruction to dye white hair—may have been shaped by the practical needs of a particular time. The task is to identify which teachings express permanent religious purposes and which are contextual applications of those purposes.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — Why inherited custom is not automatically a religious obligation

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: Explain why Mutahhari regards the different approaches of the Imams as a source of strength for Shi‘ism rather than a contradiction.
questions.answer: Mutahhari acknowledges that the Imams sometimes acted differently from one another, and that these differences can confuse followers who assume every action must be copied in exactly the same way. He argues, however, that the differences provide a wider body of guidance. If one Imam lived for only twenty or thirty years, people might not see enough examples to distinguish permanent religious principles from responses to a particular historical situation. If the same leader lived for 250 years and faced many different circumstances, followers would learn how the same religious spirit can be applied in changing conditions. The different lives of the Imams therefore reveal more of the practical range of Islam. The apparent contradictions become a strength when their contexts are researched and their underlying purposes are understood.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — How a rich tradition can guide followers and still require careful interpretation

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: How does the example of Sufyan al-Thawri and Imam al-Sadiq demonstrate the difference between copying an outward custom and following the spirit of religion?
questions.answer: Sufyan al-Thawri objected to Imam al-Sadiq’s fine clothing because the Prophet had lived simply and worn modest garments. He assumed that the Prophet’s outward lifestyle was a fixed religious command that every Muslim must follow in every age. Imam al-Sadiq explained that the Prophet’s lifestyle reflected the economic conditions of his time and his refusal to take advantage of his position. Islam’s permanent teachings concern equality, compassion, justice, and fairness, not a compulsory style of clothing. The Imam also explained that people may choose different garments according to their circumstances, provided they fulfil their responsibilities toward the poor and do not display wealth in a way that wounds others. The lesson is that following the Prophet means preserving the moral purpose of his conduct, not mechanically copying every outward feature of a historically conditioned lifestyle.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — Imam al-Sadiq on clothing, circumstance, and the spirit of religion

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: Explain how the famine incident strengthens Imam al-Sadiq’s explanation of the Prophet’s lifestyle.
questions.answer: During a famine, Imam al-Sadiq ordered his financial supervisor to sell the family’s stored wheat in the market and buy their daily bread from the same market. The ordinary bread was made from a mixture of oat and wheat, and the Imam chose to eat it rather than use the family’s stored wheat while others suffered. He explained that Islam does not prescribe one particular type of grain or bread. Its permanent commands require fairness, justice, and kindness in the way people live among others. The incident shows that the Imam’s comfortable lifestyle in ordinary times did not contradict the Prophet’s simplicity. When the community faced hardship, the Imam shared the conditions of ordinary people. The essential principle was compassion and equality, not a permanent ban on fine clothing or a fixed diet.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — Imam al-Sadiq on clothing, circumstance, and the spirit of religion

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: Explain Imam ‘Ali’s interpretation of the instruction to dye white hair and the general lesson it teaches about Prophetic traditions.
questions.answer: Mutahhari says that Imam ‘Ali narrated the Prophet’s instruction to dye white hair so that Muslims would not resemble the Jews, but ‘Ali did not personally dye his beard. He explained that the instruction had served a particular military purpose during the Prophet’s time: in battle, it made it harder for the enemy to distinguish older soldiers from younger ones. When the military circumstances changed, the practice was no longer a universal requirement. Mutahhari uses the example to show that a Prophetic instruction may be connected to a temporary need. Scholars must therefore examine the purpose and context of a tradition before turning an outward practice into a permanent religious obligation. The permanent aim is to follow divine guidance, not to preserve every historical tactic without regard to its original reason.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — Imam ‘Ali’s explanation of the beard-dyeing instruction

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: How should scholars and followers distinguish permanent religious principles from actions that were appropriate only to the circumstances of a particular Imam’s time?
questions.answer: Mutahhari argues that followers must study the sayings and actions of the Imams in their historical and social contexts. A practice may reflect the requirements of a particular period rather than a permanent command. The Prophet’s simple clothing, Imam al-Sadiq’s fine clothing, and Imam ‘Ali’s explanation of beard-dyeing show how outward conduct can differ while the underlying principles of justice, compassion, equality, and obedience to God remain the same. The method of conventional reconciliation, al-jam‘ al-‘urfi, allows scholars to examine apparently conflicting traditions by identifying their context and purpose. At the same time, Mutahhari distinguishes these contextual practices from the essence of religious teachings—divine commands based on enduring public interests—which cannot be altered. Careful study prevents extremity, rigidity, and the misuse of selected traditions to justify personal preferences.
questions.source_locator: Dissimulation (taqiyyah) — Why inherited custom is not automatically a religious obligation

questions.unit_title: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn’s Path and That of Other Imams
questions.prompt: Why does Mutahhari warn that an abundance of hadith can become a source of confusion if it is not accompanied by sound interpretation?
questions.answer: Mutahhari regards the large number of Shi‘ah traditions and supplications as a major intellectual resource. He notes the report that al-Kafi contains more than sixteen thousand traditions, although he says he has not personally counted them. However, he warns that many reports and examples from different Imams can be misused if their circumstances are ignored. People may select a particular action, treat it as an absolute rule, and use it to justify their own interests. Apparent differences between the Imams can then produce confusion, extremism, and a loss of moral direction. Mutahhari therefore says that abundant evidence must be accompanied by research, contextual understanding, and the ability to distinguish the essence of religion from the requirements of a particular time.
